extracted.intended_audience: petitioners for NRC rulemaking, applicants for standard design certification, licensees, parties and counsel participating in NRC adjudicatory proceedings (including those handling Restricted Data/National Security Information)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for petitions for rulemaking, notices of proposed rulemaking, participation and Commission action, filing and acceptance of standard design certification applications, and special procedures for handling Restricted Data and National Security Information in NRC proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of petition deficiencies and resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: If the NRC determines a petition requires further consideration but is deficient, the NRC will notify the petitioner in writing and explain the deficiencies. The petitioner may resubmit the petition for rulemaking without prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written notification must explain deficiencies; resubmission is permitted and treated without prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing criteria for petitions for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC will docket and assign a docket number to a petition only if: (i) the petition includes the information required by § 2.802(c); (ii) the regulatory change sought is within the NRC's legal authority; and (iii) the petition raises a potentially valid issue that warrants further consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three elements are conditions for docketing; cite § 2.802(c) for required petition contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting and notice of docketed petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of a docketed petition will be posted in ADAMS and on http://www.regulations.gov and the NRC will publish a notice of docketing in the Federal Register with the docket number and how the public may track status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Docketing triggers public posting (ADAMS and regs.gov) and a FR notice describing tracking information.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC communication with multiple petitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition is signed by multiple petitioners, the NRC's obligation to inform a petitioner is satisfied for all petitioners when the NRC transmits the required notification to the lead petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a lead petitioner to receive NRC notifications unless otherwise required by §2 subpart H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment posting and removal of identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC will post all comment submissions at http://www.regulations.gov and enter them into ADAMS, without removing identifying or contact information from comment submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone aggregating or soliciting comments must inform contributors not to include identifying/contact info they do not want publicly disclosed; NRC will not redact such info before posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudicatory hearings on petitions for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: No adjudicatory or legislative hearing under 10 CFR part 2 will be held on a petition for rulemaking unless the Commission determines to do so, at its discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing on petitions is discretionary and requires Commission determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors guiding NRC determination on petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: After docketing, the NRC's determination on a petition may be based on: (i) the merits of the petition; (ii) immediacy of the safety/environment/security concern; (iii) availability of NRC resources and priority relative to other rulemaking issues; (iv) whether issues are already under consideration in other NRC processes; (v) substance of any public comment received (if requested); and (vi) the NRC's relevant past decisions and current policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These considerations are illustrative, not exclusive; agency discretion informed by merits, resources, overlap, public comment, and precedent/policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative closure of petition docket and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: After determining the appropriate regulatory action, the NRC will administratively close the petition docket and publish a Federal Register notice describing the action with any related Docket ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closure follows the determination on regulatory action and is publicly announced in the FR; related docket identifiers are included as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible docket closure outcomes (denial or initiation of rulemaking)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC may close a petition docket by: (i) deciding not to undertake rulemaking and informing the petitioner in writing of the grounds for denial; or (ii) initiating a rulemaking action (new, ongoing, or planned) that considers the petition issues and informing the petitioner in writing of this decision and the associated Docket ID, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rulemaking is initiated, the petitioner will be notified and provided the Docket ID for the rulemaking action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of petition resolution in Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC will publish a Federal Register notice informing the public that it has concluded all planned regulatory action with respect to some or all issues presented in a petition—by adoption of a final rule, denial, or petition withdrawal. The notice will include discussion of how the regulatory action addresses the issue, grounds for denial, or information on withdrawal, and normally the NRC's response to any public comment received (if comment was requested).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FR notice should explain the disposition and normally include responses to public comments unless NRC indicates it will not provide formal written responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification if planned rulemaking not completed after closure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the NRC closes a petition docket because it decided to carry out a planned rulemaking but subsequently decides not to carry out the planned rulemaking to final rule publication, the NRC will notify the petitioner in writing and publish a FR notice explaining the basis for its decision; the decision will be documented as denial in the closed docket and online (ADAMS, regs.gov, Unified Agenda).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-completion is documented publicly and communicated to the petitioner as a denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of petition and rulemaking status
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC provides current information on rulemakings and petitions in the NRC Library; includes summaries in the semiannual Unified Agenda; and posts all docketed petitions, rulemakings, and public comments in ADAMS and at http://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple public sources (NRC website, Unified Agenda, ADAMS, regs.gov) provide status and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of proposed rulemaking required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of proposed rulemaking must include: (1) terms or substance of the proposed rule, or specification of subjects/issues involved; (2) manner and time for public comment and statement that copies of comments may be examined on NRC website; (3) authority under which the regulation is proposed; (4) time, place, and nature of any public hearing; (5) if hearing is to be held, designation of presiding officer and special directions for conduct; and (6) any explanatory statement the Commission considers appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mandatory content elements for NPRs absent the narrow exceptions in paragraph (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of notice prior to hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication or service of notice shall be made not less than 15 days prior to the time fixed for hearing, unless the Commission for good cause stated in the notice provides otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default minimum is 15 days' notice before hearing; Commission may shorten for good cause with explanation in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-and-comment exceptions and post-promulgation comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and comment are not required for interpretative rules, general statements of policy, or rules of agency organization/procedure/practice; or when Commission finds good cause that notice/comment are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest (reasons incorporated into the rule). For rules adopted without notice/comment under the good-cause exception when basis is 'impracticable' or 'contrary to public interest,' and for interpretative rules/general policy statements adopted without notice/comment, the Commission shall provide a 30-day post-promulgation comment period (with limited exceptions). For any post-promulgation comments received under this provision, the Commission shall publish a FR statement evaluating significant comments and any revisions made as a result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good-cause findings must be published in the rule; post-promulgation comment periods and evaluations are required in specified situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for participation in rulemaking proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In rulemaking proceedings under § 2.804(a) the Commission will afford interested persons an opportunity to participate through submission of statements, information, opinions, and arguments as stated in the notice, and may grant additional reasonable opportunity; the Commission may also hold informal hearings at which interested persons may be heard using procedures that best serve the hearing's purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation opportunities are defined by the NPR and may be expanded by the Commission to ensure adequate input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of basis and purpose in notice of adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: When adopting a regulation, the Commission will include in the notice of adoption a concise general statement of its basis and purpose and will publish the notice and regulation in the Federal Register or serve upon affected persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basis and purpose statement must be concise; publication/serving ensures notice to affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date timing and conditional sunsetting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of adoption will specify the effective date. Publication/service of the notice and regulation will be made not less than 30 days prior to the effective date unless Commission directs otherwise for good cause. Additionally, all regulations promulgated after January 8, 2026 under the Atomic Energy Act, Energy Reorganization Act, or Nuclear Waste Policy Act that are not required by statute or not part of a regulatory permitting regime must include a conditional sunset date no more than 5 years from the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default effective-date notice is 30 days; after Jan 8, 2026 certain NRC regulations must include a <=5-year conditional sunset unless statutory/permitting exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary authority to rule on procedural matters
rubrics_metrics.description: When documents are submitted to the Commission itself, the Secretary or Assistant Secretary may: (a) prescribe filing schedules (which may differ from other rules); (b) rule on motions for extensions of time; (c) reject late filings unless good cause shown; and (d) prescribe procedural arrangements for any oral argument before the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary/Assistant Secretary has delegated procedural authority to manage filings and oral argument logistics; late filings can be rejected subject to good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACRS participation in rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards (ACRS) may recommend the Commission initiate rulemaking; the Commission will respond in writing within 90 days noting intent to implement, study, or defer, providing reasons if not accepted. When a rule involving nuclear safety matters within ACRS purview is under staff development, the staff will ensure the ACRS is given opportunity to provide advice at appropriate stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACRS recommendations and Commission responses are made available on the NRC website following transmittal; staff must integrate ACRS input opportunities into rule development on safety matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC size standards for small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and thresholds: small business — service/non-manufacturing with average gross receipts of $8.0 million or less over last 5 fiscal years or manufacturing with 500 or fewer employees; small organization — not-for-profit independently owned with annual gross receipts of $8.0 million or less; small governmental jurisdiction — population <50,000; small educational institution — supported by qualifying small government or not state/publicly supported with 500 or fewer employees. NRC uses SBA definition of receipts and subsidiaries of large entities do not qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Size thresholds follow SBA rules (13 CFR 121.104); NRC provides outreach and a toll-free number for small entities seeking compliance information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of standard design certification applications (method & electronic requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The signed original application (and amendments) must be sent by mail (to Document Control Desk), facsimile, hand delivery to NRC offices (during business hours), or where practicable by electronic submission (e.g., Electronic Information Exchange, email, CD-ROM). Electronic submissions must enable NRC to receive, read, authenticate, distribute, archive, and retrieve the submission a single page at a time. Detailed e-submittal guidance is on NRC's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If paper, send signed original; follow NRC e-submittal guidance for acceptable formats and electronic signatures; consult MSHD.Resource@nrc.gov or Office of the CIO as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for standard design certification applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each original of an application and amendment must meet the requirements in § 2.813 (form of communications); the applicant must be capable of producing additional copies for distribution per written instructions of the appropriate Director; in any hearing under subpart O the applicant must make an updated application copy available for use by parties and certify that it contains current contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be able to provide public hearing copies and certify currentness; § 2.813 imposes formatting and transmission standards for written communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application consultation for standard design certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A prospective applicant may consult with NRC staff before filing by writing to the Director or calling the Regulatory Analysis and Rulemaking Support Branch toll-free; prospective applicants may confer informally with NRC staff before filing and the limitations on consultation in § 2.802(b)(2) do not apply to such pre-application consultations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre-application consultation to clarify subject matters listed in § 2.802(b)(1); toll-free assistance is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: General written communications transmission and timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence, reports, and other written communications concerning regulations in this subpart (and specified parts of the chapter) must be sent to the Document Control Desk or by hand/electronic submission as practicable; electronic submissions must meet readability and archival requirements; if a submission due date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday, the next Federal working day is the official due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified addresses and e-submittal standards; weekend/holiday deadlines shift to next Federal working day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form requirements for paper submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All paper copies must be typewritten, printed, or otherwise reproduced in permanent form on unglazed paper. Exceptions may be granted for micrographic, photographic, or similar forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper submissions should be permanent and legible; request exceptions where justified for nonstandard media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation practice on submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant submitting correspondence or reports is requested but not required to cite, when practical, in the upper right corner of the first page, the specific regulation or other basis requiring submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing the governing regulation is encouraged to aid processing but is not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing and acceptance review for design certification applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application will be assigned a docket number; initially each application will be treated as tendered to determine completeness and acceptability for docketing, with a copy of the tendered application available for public inspection. Generally, determination on acceptability will be made within 30 days. The Commission may base acceptability on technical adequacy as well as completeness. If acceptable, a docket number is assigned and applicant notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a ~30-day initial review; completeness and technical adequacy both inform docketing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of standard design certification application
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may permit an applicant to withdraw an application before issuance of a notice of proposed rulemaking on terms it prescribes, or may deny or dismiss a withdrawal request without prejudice. NRC will publish in the Federal Register a document withdrawing the application if prior notices were published. Withdrawal does not authorize removal of any document from Commission files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal is possible before NPR issuance but does not erase records; publication practice depends on prior notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of application for failure to supply requested information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may deny an application if an applicant fails to respond to a request for additional information within 30 days (or other specified time). If denied for failure to respond timely, NRC will publish a notice of denial in the Federal Register and notify the applicant with a simple statement of the grounds. If prior notices were on the NRC website, the action will also be published on the website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely response to information requests (typically within 30 days) is required to avoid denial; denial will be publicly announced with grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Subpart I (safeguarding Restricted Data and NSI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures issued to effectively safeguard and prevent disclosure of Restricted Data and National Security Information to unauthorized persons while minimizing impairment of procedural rights in proceedings subject to this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance security safeguarding with protection of procedural rights; Subpart I provides the procedures to achieve that balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Subpart I
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies, as applicable, to all proceedings under subparts G, J, K, L, M, and N of this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Subpart I procedures whenever proceedings fall within those listed subparts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key definitions for Restricted Data/NSI procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions include: government agency; interested party (party having interest in issue to which Restricted Data/NSI is relevant, usually determinable from notice of hearing and pleadings); 'introduced into a proceeding' (incorporation of testimony or documentary matter into the official record); National Security Information (classified pursuant to Executive Order 12356); and party (includes persons admitted under §2.309 or interested States under §2.315(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions guide who may seek access and what counts as introduction into the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: General protection obligation for RD/NSI
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in Subpart I relieves any person from safeguarding Restricted Data or National Security Information in accordance with applicable U.S. laws and rules/regulations/orders of any Government Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties remain bound by all statutory/regulatory safeguarding obligations irrespective of these procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification assistance by Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of any party or presiding officer, the Commission will designate a representative to advise and assist the presiding officer and parties regarding security classification of information and safeguards to be observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek Commission-designated assistance when classification or safeguard questions arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to RD/NSI introduced into proceedings (who may access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restricted Data or National Security Information introduced into a proceeding will be made available to any interested party having the required security clearance, to counsel for an interested party with required clearance, and to additional persons with required clearance as determined necessary by the Commission or presiding officer for adequate preparation/presentation. Action on applications may be postponed until after notice of hearing, answers, and replies are filed where party interest will not be prejudiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is clearance-dependent and limited to those necessary for case preparation; timing of access orders can be adjusted to protect interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to RD/NSI not introduced into proceedings (application process)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party showing that access may be required for case preparation may apply for access; the Commission or presiding officer will issue an order granting access upon obtaining required security clearances. For information received from another Government agency, applications are acted upon by the Commission. Applications should describe subject, classification level, stage of proceeding, reasons for access, names of individuals for clearances, and reasons for those clearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed unclassified description in application to expedite consideration; expect different processing when info originates from another agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission handling of security clearance requests and charges
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will consider requests for appropriate security clearances in reasonable numbers and will make a reasonable charge for costs of security clearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for administrative processing time and possible fees when requesting clearances for multiple individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and appeals concerning access orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may certify questions relating to access to the Commission for determination. Any party affected by a presiding officer's determination/order may appeal forthwith to the Commission. Filing by staff of an appeal from an order granting access stays the order pending Commission determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding-officer decisions on access can be escalated quickly; staff appeals stay access orders pending resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and disposal of classified matter after proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: On conclusion of a proceeding, the Commission will terminate all orders and security clearances issued in the proceeding and may issue orders requiring disposal of classified matter received pursuant to them or requiring other safeguarding procedures as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearances and access orders are time-limited to the proceeding; expect disposal/safeguarding directives at conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to grant access to RD/NSI
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will not grant access unless it determines granting access will not be inimical to the common defense and security. Access to RD/NSI received from another Government agency will not be granted if the originating agency determines in writing that access should not be granted; the Commission will consult with the originating agency before granting access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security considerations and originating-agency determinations control access decisions; the Commission must conclude access is safe from national-defense/security standpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to avoid introducing RD/NSI where practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties in proceedings are obligated to avoid, where practicable, introducing Restricted Data or National Security Information into the proceeding, regardless of whether other parties have required clearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should seek alternatives (e.g., redactions, unclassified summaries) to avoid classified disclosures when practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intent requirements when classified matter likely
rubrics_metrics.description: If staff or a party believes it will be impracticable to avoid introducing RD/NSI, they must file a notice of intent (staff at time of publication of notice of hearing; parties in answers or when the need arises later) informing other parties. RD/NSI shall not be introduced after publication of a notice of hearing unless a notice of intent has been filed per § 2.908, except as permitted by the presiding officer when no prejudice results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely unclassified notice of intent is required to preserve procedural fairness and allow clearances to be sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of notice of intent to introduce classified matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of intent must be unclassified and include: (1) subject matter of RD/NSI anticipated; (2) highest classification level of the information; (3) stage of proceeding at which information may be introduced; and (4) the relevance and materiality of the information to the issues in the proceeding. The presiding officer may allow such notice to be given orally on the record in their discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient unclassified detail to permit evaluation and clearance planning; oral notices may be permitted when consistent with fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rearrangement or suspension of proceedings for clearance acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party gives notice of intent to introduce classified matter and the presiding officer determines another interested party lacks required clearances, the presiding officer may: (a) rearrange the proceeding order to allow time to obtain clearances with minimal delay; (b) suspend the proceeding or portion thereof until clearances obtained (no more than 100 days unless consent or further suspension not contrary to public interest); or (c) take other actions deemed in best interest of parties/public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officer has discretion to manage scheduling and temporary suspensions to accommodate security clearance processes, subject to limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit unclassified statements when classified matter is introduced
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever RD/NSI is introduced, the party offering it must submit to the presiding officer and all parties an unclassified statement setting forth the information in the classified matter as accurately and completely as possible (to the extent consistent with classification). The presiding officer may determine whether such an unclassified statement or modified version may be substituted for the classified matter without prejudice; if adequate, the classified matter shall be excluded from the record. If inadequate, the presiding officer shall include reasons in the record. Service of the unclassified statement should not be postponed if any party lacks access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the unclassified statement mechanism to maximize public record while protecting classified information; presiding officer decides adequacy and possible exclusion of classified material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility standards for classified evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A presiding officer shall not receive any RD/NSI in evidence unless (a) the relevance and materiality to issues and competence are clearly established; and (b) exclusion of the classified information would prejudice the interests of a party or the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified evidence must meet standard relevance/competence thresholds and exclusion must create prejudice to justify admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight to be attached to classified evidence when access limited
rubrics_metrics.description: When classified evidence is received to which an interested party has not had opportunity to receive access, the presiding officer and Commission shall give such evidence such weight as is appropriate under the circumstances, considering any lack of opportunity to rebut or impeach the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited access may reduce evidentiary weight; decisionmakers must account for inability to rebut when assessing probative value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and possible expungement of classified matter from the record
rubrics_metrics.description: At close of reception of evidence, the presiding officer shall review the record and direct that any RD/NSI be expunged from the record where such expunction would not prejudice the interests of a party or the public interest. Such directions will be considered by the Commission on review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer must balance privacy/security against prejudice/public interest before ordering expungement; expungement orders enter the record for Commission review.
